idiom_name: ASP.NET Core authentication middleware + registered authentication schemes
implementation_notes: ASP.NET Core ships the checkpoint as middleware: UseAuthentication() runs the authentication service, which dispatches to the registered scheme's handler (JWT bearer, cookie, OIDC) - the delegated, replaceable mechanism - and populates HttpContext.User; protection itself is an authorization policy (FallbackPolicy or [Authorize]/RequireAuthorization) that invokes the scheme's challenge for unauthenticated requests. Custom code is only warranted for a new mechanism (implement IAuthenticationHandler), never to re-implement the middleware. The classic interceptor structure is absorbed by the framework, so configuration plus a handler implementation replaces it.
code_sketch:
builder.Services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
    .AddJwtBearer(o => builder.Configuration.Bind("Jwt", o));         // mechanism
builder.Services.AddAuthorization(o => o.FallbackPolicy =
    new AuthorizationPolicyBuilder().RequireAuthenticatedUser().Build());  // default deny
var app = builder.Build();
app.UseAuthentication();   // checkpoint: builds HttpContext.User from the scheme
app.UseAuthorization();    // enforces the policy -> challenge on failure
app.MapGet("/orders", (ClaimsPrincipal user) => Orders.For(user));
pitfalls: UseAuthentication() alone protects nothing: it only populates HttpContext.User, so without a fallback policy or [Authorize]/RequireAuthorization every endpoint stays anonymous.
Middleware order matters: the authentication middleware must run before anything that reads HttpContext.User, otherwise later components see an anonymous principal.
Registering several schemes without naming a default makes the first challenge undefined (InvalidOperationException: no DefaultAuthenticateScheme), so set the default scheme explicitly.
